$D_5\subseteq\Omega_{\mu-1}$: the third invariant of $Q_{ab}$Let $Q$ be a finite $3$-group of class $\le4$ and $\mu\ge0$ such that at most two invariants of $Q/\gamma_2(Q)$ exceed $3^\mu$ (e.g. $3^\mu$ the third largest invariant). Then $z^{3^{\mu-1}}=1$ for every $z\in D_5(Q)$ (with $3^{\mu-1}:=1$ for $\mu=0$). In particular, if at most two invariants of $Q/\gamma_2(Q)$ are $\ge9$, then $D_5(Q)=1$, with no condition on $\gamma_4(Q)$. · Lean · D_five_pow_eq_one_of_third_invariant, D_five_eq_bot_of_two_large_invariantsNot in the paper: the proof on paper is Theorem 12.6 of wiki 891 §12.3 (MATH-451, reviewed per 703) with its case μ ≤ 1, Theorem 11.2 (§11.2, MATH-450); the Lean proof is group-dimension#54 (MATH-468). It evaluates the exact identity (⋆) (Star.two_smul_gen_eq, node own:ab399) term by term after multiplying by 3^{μ-1}. In Lean the hypothesis is stated intrinsically: the 3^μ-th powers of Q_ab contain at most 9 elements of order dividing 3. The conclusion is the exponent bound on D_5(Q); together with D_5(Q) ⊆ γ_4(Q)^3 (Corollary 6.12) it gives D_5(Q) ⊆ Ω_{μ-1}(γ_4(Q)), but that combination is not stated in Lean. The case μ = 1 contains the type [3,9,9] of own:ab399. Only the finite form of class ≤ 4 is in Lean; the general form D_5(G) = γ_5(G) is not formalized.
